title: Eve — A Production Agent Is Just a Folder of Files

EVE // OPS BRIEF / A Production Agent Is Just a Folder of Files 01 / 13 · THESIS
Verdict  ·  2026  ·  Vercel Ship London
A production agent is now
just a folder of files.
Vercel’s Eve is “Next.js for agents” — Markdown for instructions and skills, TypeScript for tools, durable by default. eve build compiles a directory into a deployed service.

OPS BRIEF · CONFIDENTIAL · For technical leaders evaluating agent stacks Slide 01

EVE // OPS BRIEF / The Shift, Up Front 02 / 13
The shift, up front
Three ideas collapse the build‑vs‑reliability trade-off.
Filesystem‑first ease meets production‑grade rigor — without picking one.
01
The agent IS a directory.
Instructions, skills, tools, subagents and channels are just files at conventional paths. agent/  IS  the source of truth.
FILE-SYSTEM · CONVENTION
02
One eve build wires it all.
Discovers files, validates types, compiles a single manifest of tools, skills and channels. No imports. No registration. No glue.
COMPILE · MANIFEST
03
Production ships in the box.
Durability. Sandbox. Human approvals. Evals as a deploy gate. One vercel deploy — same directory, live over HTTP + Slack.
DURABLE · GATED · DEPLOYED
PATTERN > PRODUCT · Directory-as-agent Slide 02

EVE // OPS BRIEF / The Old Trade-off 03 / 13
Before Eve
You picked easy or you picked production.
You didn’t get both.
OPTION A · FILESYSTEM-FIRST
Easy. Personal‑scale.
A folder of files. Add a Markdown file, get a capability. Great on a laptop.
What’s missing
✕  Durability
✕  Sandbox
✕  Approvals
✕  Evals
✕  Deploy target
✕  Multi‑channel
OPTION B · PRODUCTION FRAMEWORK
Reliable. Heavy to wire.
Real durability and controls — if you accept the vendor’s runtime, SDKs and lock‑in.
What you pay in
•  Registration boilerplate
•  Runtime lock‑in
•  SDK sprawl
•  Ops config
•  Weeks of glue
•  Migration risk
Eve’s move:  keep the ease of the folder — put the production layer in the box. The trade-off is gone.
DIAGNOSIS · Why builders had to choose Slide 03

EVE // OPS BRIEF / The Agent Is a Directory 04 / 13
Model  ·  Convention over configuration
Each capability is a file at a known path.
agent/  —  source of truth
agent/
├── instructions.md            # always-on prompt
├── tools/
│   ├── run_sql.ts             # => tool "run_sql"
│   ├── list_orders.ts
│   └── post_to_slack.ts
├── skills/
│   ├── refund-policy.md       # on-demand playbook
│   └── sql-style-guide.md
├── subagents/
│   └── reviewer.ts            # own context
└── channels/
    ├── http.ts
    ├── slack.ts
    ├── discord.ts
    └── github.ts
instructions.md
Always‑on system prompt
The agent’s identity, rules and defaults — one Markdown file.
tools/*.ts
One typed TypeScript function per file
Filename becomes the tool name. run_sql.ts ⇒ tool run_sql. Nothing to register.
skills/*.md
Markdown playbooks, loaded on demand
Domain knowledge kept out of the base prompt — pulled in when it’s needed.
subagents/*.ts
Child agents with their own context
Delegate scoped work — a reviewer, a planner — without polluting the parent’s window.
channels/*.ts
Entry points: HTTP · Slack · Discord · GitHub
PATH = CAPABILITY · FILENAME = NAME Slide 04

EVE // OPS BRIEF / One Build Wires It 05 / 13
Compile step
eve build discovers, validates, compiles — one manifest.
Input
The agent/ directory
agent/
├─ instructions.md
├─ tools/         (N files)
├─ skills/        (N files)
├─ subagents/     (N files)
└─ channels/      (N files)
FILES ON DISK
Step
$ eve build
01Discover — walk conventional paths
02Validate — TypeScript types + schemas
03Compile — emit one wired manifest
04Bind — channels → tools → skills
Output
One manifest
{
  "tools":    [ … ],
  "skills":   [ … ],
  "channels": [ … ],
  "subagents":[ … ]
}
WIRED & TYPED
Convention over configuration
File location = capability
Filename = tool name
No imports to keep in sync
No glue to maintain
ZERO REGISTRATION · ZERO CEREMONY Slide 05

EVE // OPS BRIEF / Production In The Box 06 / 13
Runtime · Deploy
The reliability layer ships with the framework.
01 · Durable sessions
Checkpointed workflow — survives crashes and redeploys.
Restarts resume exactly where they stopped. Long-running agents stop being fragile.
02 · Vercel Sandbox
Agent‑written code runs isolated — off your machine.
Untrusted code stays in a controlled runtime, not your laptop or a shared shell.
03 · Approvals
Human-in-the-loop, native.
Risky tool calls pause and wait for a human Allow. Built in, not bolted on.
04 · Evals
Deploy gate, not an afterthought.
Evals sit on the deploy path. Regressions stop the release before users see them.
05 · One deploy
vercel deploy — live over HTTP & Slack.
Same directory, prod.
Net:  the operational surface an internal team actually needs — delivered as defaults, not homework.
DURABLE · SANDBOXED · GATED · EVALUATED · DEPLOYED Slide 06

EVE // OPS BRIEF / You Don’t Hand-Code It 07 / 13
Author workflow  ·  Coding agent as builder
Scaffold, build, test, deploy — by prompting.
One command
$  npx plugins add vercel/vercel-plugin
Knowledge
47+

Over a relational knowledge graph of Eve’s APIs and patterns.
Delegation

Specialist agents
Scoped sub‑agents your coding assistant can hand work to.
Ergonomics

Slash commands
Shortcuts for the common scaffold‑test‑ship loop.
Correctness
Real-time
Code validation
Wrong shapes fail as you type — before you ship.
Verdict
One plugin turns your coding agent into an Eve builder. The framework isn’t what you learn — it’s what your assistant already knows.
PROMPT > TYPE · Meta‑tooling in the box Slide 07

EVE // OPS BRIEF / Human In The Loop 09 / 13
Gate  ·  Trust boundary
Full power — gated exactly where it counts.
#analytics  ·  eve‑analyst · SLACK
@dana  ·  10:42
run SELECT * FROM order_items
⚠ approval required
Full-table scan detected on order_items (194 rows)
query: SELECT * FROM order_items;
Waiting for a human Allow before running. Nothing has executed.
ALLOW
DENY
status: PENDING  ·  workflow paused  ·  durable checkpoint held
The trust boundary
The setup that lets an internal team trust an agent in production.
✓Risky tool calls pause automatically
✓Approval happens in the channel — not a console
✓Workflow resumes exactly where it paused
✓The reviewer — and the decision — is logged
Discipline
Locking the agent down so it cannot act is safe — and useless.
Approvals let you keep the power on, and put a human on the trigger where it matters.
APPROVAL AS FIRST‑CLASS PRIMITIVE Slide 09

EVE // OPS BRIEF / Where Eve Sits 10 / 13
Landscape  ·  Filesystem-first bet
A filesystem‑first bet in a fast‑filling field.
Framework Language Runtime Durability Position
Eve / Vercel TypeScript Vercel-only Default Deep Vercel integration
Mastra TypeScript Any host Add-on Platform‑agnostic
LangGraph Python Any host Configurable Most established
Inngest AgentKit TypeScript Any host Default Durable workflows
The cost
Eve trades portability for integration.
Vercel-only today. Rivals run anywhere.
The bet
The directory‑as‑agent pattern is the bet — not necessarily Eve itself.
Adopt the pattern; keep the vendor decision reversible.
PATTERN OVER PRODUCT Slide 10

EVE // OPS BRIEF / Read The Fine Print 11 / 13
Timing call
Move now — or wait? Both cases are real.
Move now
The pattern will win.
✓ Where production agents are heading.
Directory-as-agent is the direction of travel.
✓ Reliability layer is genuinely in the box.
Durability, sandbox, approvals, evals — defaults, not homework.
✓ One plugin makes it fast to try.
Prompt your coding agent into a working Eve app.
Wait
Beta receipts to read.
! Vercel-only at launch.
No other runtime today — portability isn’t on offer.
! Public beta with moving APIs.
Expect churn between releases.
! “Scale” is design intent, not a benchmark.
No published load or SLO numbers yet.
! Launch coverage was vendor-framed.
Independent field reports are still thin.
NO HEDGING — JUST THE TWO LEDGERS Slide 11

EVE // OPS BRIEF / The Move 12 / 13
Playbook
Pilot the pattern on one bounded workflow.
Clear owner. Slack surface. Rules encoded as skills. Risky calls gated by approvals and evals.
01
Pick
One bounded internal workflow.
Clear owner. Real users. Slack as the surface. Not a customer-facing agent — yet.
02
Build
Instructions + typed tools + one skill.
instructions.md  +  a few tools/*.ts  +  one skills/*.md. Let the plugin scaffold.
03
Encode
Rules that must stay consistent → Markdown.
Refund policy, SQL style, escalation path. One .md per rule — readable, review-able, diffable.
04
Gate & widen
Approvals + eval suite before widening access.
Risky actions require a human click. An eval suite blocks regressions on deploy. Then open the door.
Ship a pilot in weeks, not a platform in quarters.
ONE OWNER · ONE SURFACE · ONE GATE Slide 12
